content.title: French Quarter Fest 2026 expands into new Riverfront Park
content.text: The annual festival, which in recent years has drawn nearly a million people to the French Quarter, will feature new and expanded spaces along the riverfront. NEW ORLEANS — French Quarter Fest 2026 is just four days away, and organizers say the decades-old celebration continues to grow while staying rooted in its mission to celebrate one of the city's oldest neighborhoods. The annual festival, which in recent years has drawn nearly a million people to the French Quarter, will feature new and expanded spaces along the riverfront, including Goldring–Woldenberg Riverfront Park. “We have some incredible talent, everybody from Irma Thomas to Big Freedia, old and new, and everything in between will be playing right here," said Emily Madero, President and CEO of French Quarter Festivals Inc. Madero said the expanded park will offer more than just music. She noted food and beverage vendors will line the area near the train tracks, while a children’s playground will be located on the opposite side of the park, making the festival more family-friendly. “We definitely encourage families to come out. Bring your picnic blanket, bring your hammocks—there are even places to install them.” The Abita Beer and Tropical Isle Hand Grenade stages will also be at the new park. Across Esplanade Avenue near the New Orleans Jazz Museum, the Pan-American Life Insurance Group Stage will continue to highlight world music, adding to the festival’s diverse lineup. Madero emphasized that the festival remains rooted in its nonprofit mission, founded more than four decades ago. “First and foremost, we are a nonprofit,” she said. “We were founded 43 years ago with this mission in mind. We are for New Orleans, by New Orleans. Our mission is to celebrate and uplift our local culture and bring world-class performances to the whole community in a way that everybody will participate.” Madero said the festival also serves as a reminder to residents to experience their own city. “We often take for granted the incredible history and architecture,” she said. “This is a neighborhood like nowhere else in the world. It’s a good reminder to come be a tourist in our own city.” French Quarter Fest spans multiple days and stages throughout the French Quarter, and Madero said the event is the result of year-round planning from staff and volunteers. “I get excited every year once we start to build the assets and it comes to life,” she said. “It is a labor of love. We work all year round with an incredible team and volunteer board, and seeing it come together is so rewarding.” The festival opens Thursday morning with its traditional kickoff parade down Bourbon Street and a ceremony in Jackson Square. French Quarter Fest 2026 runs Thursday through Sunday.
